findings.reason: without a discriminating case the node's gate cannot show the lease rule is doing the work, and the control as written would report success while the defect it names is present.
findings.text: §2's negative control is "with the function replaced by one keyed on process age, the resumed-session case must fail", but the resumed session in that case has a fresh lease and therefore a fresh process, so process-age keying also reads it live and the case passes; the stated mutation cannot produce the failure the control claims

findings.reason: half the section's deliverable is unverifiable, and the cause is what decides whether the repair targets the right mechanism.
findings.text: §8's first deliverable, "a written cause, in this plan's landed record", is measured by nothing in the done-when, which only asserts the repaired obligations list; a worker can pass the gate having written no cause

findings.reason: one node cannot be closed on a partial result, so a worker that lands one half and is blocked on the other leaves the section neither closable nor re-dispatchable.
findings.text: §6 delivers two unrelated capabilities: scheduler job comments carrying session and run ids, and a directory view carrying a peer name and a reachable flag; they share no surface and no test

findings.reason: the two nodes would ship contradictory behaviour for the same record and a reader could not tell which retirement happened.
findings.text: §4 raises a decision covering "every record the session owns" including awaiting-upstream requests, while §5 retires any stranded awaiting-upstream request outright; a stranded request owned by a lost session is claimed by both sections, neither declares the other, and no rule says which acts first or whether the decision is written for a record §5 then deletes

findings.reason: the repair and its base-arm control both target a comparison the source does not contain, so a worker either ships a no-op guard or returns blocked after its base arm passes.
findings.text: §8 blames an obligation row drawn with the reason "Not this session's run: owner session 0f4fa699" against the run's own owner, but that text is emitted by no code in this tree: a search of `reckon/`, `tests/` and `docs/ui/` for "Not this session" and "owner session" finds only a docstring in `reckon/crew/session_host.py:431`, while the phrase exists verbatim in a stored acknowledgement reason (`~/.config/reckon/crew/acknowledgements/r-20261117T225500180499-fit-inside-the-iteration.json`); the plan's own evidence — the row appearing "five to seven times" — is the shape of a stored deferral re-raised, not of an owner comparison

findings.reason: §9's done-when resolves the record by project (`crew view live --project concurrent-dispatch-fixture`), so the truncated id does not misdirect a worker.
findings.text: the stray pointer §9 cites is written `r-20261117T093219…node-one-worktree`, truncated with an ellipsis, so it names no record a later reader can open

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §8's quoted obligation reason does not resolve to any emitter in this tree, and §9 cites a truncated run id.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's negative control cannot fail the case it names, and §8's "written cause" deliverable has no check.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate the sections name is a test file under `tests/` plus the plan's own landed record; no scratchpad, node-local temporary or session-only path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach a named symbol, file or comment, and no section states a changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8's stated cause (an obligation row drawn with a not-yours reason against its own owner) is not the mechanism the cited evidence supports.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §6 carries two independent deliverables (a scheduler comment field and a directory-view peer address) in one node.
